title: Stores in Japan Lower Prices for Rice-Based Products
paragraphs: In Japan, the price of rice has been very high for a long time. But now, rice prices are falling, and some stores are lowering the prices of their rice products.
Japan's three biggest convenience store chains have announced lower prices for onigiri, or rice balls. Onigiri are a popular snack in Japan, and they are sold at every convenience store.

From September 29, Lawson lowered the price of its Temaki Onigiri by 10 yen. For example, its tuna mayonnaise onigiri went down from 181 yen to 171 yen, and its grilled salmon onigiri went down from 221 yen to 211 yen. In total, 20 types of onigiri are now cheaper.
7-Eleven also said it would lower the price of its salmon and mentaiko onigiri by 19 yen, from 214 yen. FamilyMart also lowered the prices of some of its onigiri.

The stores are lowering prices because rice has become cheaper. According to Japan's agriculture ministry, the average price of a 5-kilogram bag of rice at supermarkets fell by 27.7% between the start of this year and the middle of August. By September, the average price was below 3,000 yen for the first time in two years.

In the past, most onigiri cost about 120 to 140 yen. But when rice prices went up, the stores raised their onigiri prices again and again. Many onigiri now cost about twice as much as they did a few years ago.
The new prices are still higher than before, but many shoppers are happy to see them go down.
